**LESSON (external ruling rev 4, #297, finding R297-RULING-MECHANISM-GAP): a ruling may assert the PROPERTY, but naming the MECHANISM inherits the same run-don't-assert bar as everyone else's claims.**

**What happened**: the rev-3 ruling on #297 stated the right invariant — "a tree-keyed offender whose own payload is present at the audited tip can never be exempted" — and bound it to `exempt = isResolvedAt(candidate, auditedTip).resolved && netAddFull(candidate) <= 0`. Implemented verbatim, it turned green the two fixtures the ruling discussed (A7, A8) and broke two it never mentioned (A2, A6): `isResolvedAt` sums the half-open `(candidate, tip]`, which is EMPTY for every tip-most merge, so `resolved:false` came back categorically — denying the exemption to exactly the legitimate tip-most cleanup reverters the mechanism exists to serve.

**Why it survived review**: mechanism bindings are held to a lower evidentiary standard than the claims around them. A finding carries evidence and a fix carries a test, but the clause that says "implement it as f(x) && g(y)" travels on fluency with the code — and fluency is what a degenerate range defeats. The range asymmetry was documented in the module and still misread.

**Two structural amplifiers**: (1) a ruling is downstream of the frozen tests but is not checked against them — the reviewer reasoned about the fixtures named in the escalation, not the frozen set as a whole; (2) its verdict is socially load-bearing, so the cheapest response to "the ruling breaks two fixtures" is to weaken the two fixtures.

**The correct response, which is the part worth keeping**: the correction went into the RULING, not into the fixtures. #297 recorded the gap as a `correction` finding against its own prior revision and re-ruled as (c′). The frozen set is the spec; neither implementer nor reviewer edits the spec to make an error fit. Cost: one escalation, instead of a silently weakened guard.

**Applies to**: any review verdict, ruling, or design note that names a specific function, predicate, flag, or range as the way to satisfy a property — reviewer output as much as author output.

**Promotion candidate** (ADR-0013 draft-and-promote): the long-form anti-pattern draft lives at `openspec/changes/issue-259-d2/brain-drafts/ruling-bound-to-an-unrun-mechanism.md`, awaiting the owner's promotion into `brain/core/anti-patterns/`.
